newsitem.title: TAIWAN: China Steel sells 203 mln shares in GDRs.
newsitem.headline: China Steel sells 203 mln shares in GDRs.

text.p: China Steel Corp, Taiwan's largest steelmaker, has released 203 million shares to foreign investors through issuance of global depositary receipts abroad, the economics ministry said on Tuesday.
The move scaled down the Taiwan government's holdings in China Steel to 3.089 billion shares, or 42.89 percent of the company's total stake, the ministry said in a statement.
The underwriting price was T$25.20 per share, it said.
China Steel, previously state-run, was privatised in April 1995.
China Steel's share price ended at T$25.5 on Monday before the stock market closed for the seven-day Chinese lunar new year holiday.
The ministry said the government would continue to sell off shares in state companies to bolster the economy and recharge the treasury.
"We hope the privatisation (of state companies) will benefit domestic industry and state treasury," it said.
The government has said it would release some 800 million state-owned shares worth some T$100 billion in fiscal 1997/98 (July/June) to alleviate its budget deficit. (US$1 = T$27.5)
